name: TRANSPOSE
description: TRANSPOSE converts a vertical range into a horizontal one, or a horizontal range into a vertical one, effectively flipping rows and columns.
tldr: Flips rows and columns of an array.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array of values to transpose.

basicExample.description: Turn a column into a row
basicExample.result: A horizontal row of the three values
basicExample.explanation: The three-row, one-column range becomes a one-row, three-column result.

advancedExamples.title: Rotate a table
advancedExamples.explanation: Rows become columns and columns become rows in the output.

advancedExamples.title: Feed a transposed range to another function
advancedExamples.scenario: Need rows as columns for a lookup
advancedExamples.result: Horizontal array usable by the next function
advancedExamples.explanation: The transposed array can be passed directly into functions that expect the other orientation.

howItWorks: TRANSPOSE swaps the row and column indices of the input array, so element (r, c) in the source appears at (c, r) in the result. In Microsoft 365 it spills the full result automatically; in older Excel it must be entered as an array formula across the target range.

howToSteps.name: Select the target shape
howToSteps.text: Pick a target range with swapped dimensions (rows become columns).

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: In modern Excel just type =TRANSPOSE(range); in legacy Excel select the output range, type the formula, and press Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

howToSteps.name: Confirm the result
howToSteps.text: The flipped array appears in the target range.

limitations: In older Excel, TRANSPOSE must be entered as an array formula (Ctrl+Shift+Enter); a single cell shows only one element.
The output range must have the transposed dimensions or results are truncated.
Transposing only flips orientation; it does not reshape to arbitrary dimensions.

commonErrors.cause: Legacy Excel without array entry, or the formula placed in a single cell.
commonErrors.fix: Select the full target range and use Ctrl+Shift+Enter (or use Microsoft 365's dynamic arrays).

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TRANSPOSE works the same in Google Sheets and spills automatically into the needed range.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same behavior as Excel; Sheets handles array output natively.

faq.question: Do I need Ctrl+Shift+Enter?
faq.answer: Only in older Excel; Microsoft 365 and Google Sheets spill the result automatically.

faq.question: What does TRANSPOSE do to a 2x3 range?
faq.answer: It returns a 3x2 range with rows and columns swapped.

faq.question: Can it reshape data arbitrarily?
faq.answer: No, it only flips rows and columns; the total element count is unchanged.
